about: Rows of input and expected output for how Spec of Record hashes code and writes the lock (SPEC section 11). Any implementation of the tool runs every row. The expected texts are written by hand and the hashes are computed with SHA-256 alone, never with the tool. A line in a row is one string; a text is one string. Run them with tools/test_sor_vectors.py.

style_of.how: style_of(path) -> style: the style of the lower-cased file name if it is one of the known names, else of the text after its last dot if the name has a dot, else "safe". A style is family[-keep][+kinds]; see SPEC section 11.

a script called build is not bazel
nor is a file called workspace
a Dockerfile is known by its name

a makefile is known by its name and is safe
erlang is not listed for hashing
a dot only in the folder

a name that is only an extension
the table, by exact name: BUILD
the table, by exact name: WORKSPACE

code_hash.how: code_hash(regions) -> hash: regions sorted by (file, start), each normalized by style_of(file), joined with "\n\u0000\n", SHA-256 of the UTF-8, first 12 hex digits.

rows.name: two regions of a file are joined in line order, whatever order they are given in
regions of several files are joined in file order, each by the rule of its type
the same text in one region or two gives different hashes (the join counts)
no regions is the hash of an empty text
a region of only comments and blanks is the hash of an empty text
a shell and a Python file of one clause

text_hash.how: text_hash(text) -> hash: SHA-256 of the UTF-8, first 12 hex digits (lock.h).

rows.name: a part face with a value

targets_digest.how: digest(targets) -> hash: text_hash of the lines "<target>:<code>" in the order of the target names, joined by LF. It is the `code` of a clause that keeps its code per target.

rows.name: targets in the order of their names, whatever order they come in
code in no target is the target `*`

fold.how: fold(file entries) -> entries: a line of kind "code" goes into the entry named by its `of` as targets[<target>] = {code, built}, and that entry gets code = digest(targets); a line without its clause is dropped.

rows.name: a line goes into its clause and the clause gets the digest of its targets as its code
a clause that keeps one joined code is left as it is
a line whose clause is not in the file is dropped

marker.how: parse_marker(path, line, starters) -> null | {code, words}: a marker is `@clause` after a comment starter, the whole line or after code (a line marker). Every file has the starters // # /* <!-- -- ; as runs (// and ///, ; and ;;), its type adds more (SPEC section 10), and `starters` are those its target declares, which add and never take away. Words are what follows `@clause` without a closing */ --> or *); REM and :: count only at the start of a line.

rows.name: a doubled starter is the whole marker
code before the marker makes it a line marker
a word that only starts with clause is not the marker
a quote before the word is not a starter in a javascript file
batch rem only at the start of a line
ocaml comment: the closing star paren is not an id
percent in a type that does not list it
percent in a type nobody listed
a declared starter is a run
a declared starter of two characters
a declared starter adds and takes nothing away

lock_render.how: render(entries, fmt) -> text of the lock file (fmt null: the format the entries need, 2 when a clause has `targets`, else 1): a clause with `targets` loses `targets` and `code` and gets a line `<clause>@<target>` of kind "code" per target; keys sorted, one entry per line, entry keys sorted, separators ", " and ": ", non-ASCII as written; a fmt above 1 opens with its marker line.

rows.name: sorted keys, one entry per line, entry keys sorted
non-ascii is written as it is
a test entry with a result
no entries is an empty line between the braces
a later format opens with its marker, then the entries as before
a clause with code per target: its own line without code, then a line for each target
the format follows the entries: none with a line is format 1 with no marker
